questions.prompt: In the simple pendulum experiment, the bob should be displaced through a small angle (about 10 degrees or less) because

options.text: the motion is then approximately simple harmonic
a large angle makes the bob heavier
a small angle reduces the length of the string
the period depends mainly on the angle

questions.explanation: The formula T = 2 pi sqrt(l/g) holds for small angles. For large angles the motion departs from simple harmonic motion.

questions.prompt: In Hooke's law experiment, the extension is 2 cm for each 1 N added, within the elastic limit. The spring constant is
questions.explanation: k = F / x = 1 / 0.02 = 50 N/m. Using 2 cm without conversion gives 0.5 N/cm, which is not in SI units.

questions.prompt: To find a spring's extension correctly, the original length should be measured

options.text: with the spring lying on the table unloaded
after the largest load has been removed, ignoring the hanger
with the empty hanger attached and the spring straight
at any time, since the original length is not needed

questions.explanation: The hanger always loads the spring, so the reference length includes it. A spring measured lying flat is not straight under the same conditions.

questions.prompt: A metre rule is pivoted at the 50 cm mark. A 100 g mass hangs at the 20 cm mark, and an unknown mass at the 70 cm mark balances it. The unknown mass is
questions.explanation: Moments balance: 100 x 30 = m x 20, so m = 150 g. The 67 g value inverts the distances. The unknown mass hangs nearer the pivot (20 cm against 30 cm), so it must be heavier than 100 g, which rules out 100 g and 67 g.

questions.prompt: The centre of gravity of a uniform metre rule lies at the
questions.explanation: A uniform rule's weight acts at its midpoint, which is the 50 cm mark on a metre rule. This is also the pivot position used in balance experiments. The 0 cm and 100 cm marks are the ends, and 25 cm is a quarter point. None of them is the midpoint.

questions.prompt: An inclined plane makes an angle of 30 degrees with the horizontal. Its velocity ratio (for a smooth plane) is
questions.explanation: VR = 1 / sin(theta) = 1 / 0.5 = 2. The value 0.5 is sin 30, which inverts the ratio. The value 30 is the angle itself, not a ratio, and 1.73 is tan 60.

questions.prompt: A pulley system with a velocity ratio of 4 lifts a load of 80 N with an effort of 25 N. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: MA = 80 / 25 = 3.2, so efficiency = MA / VR x 100 = 3.2 / 4 = 80%. An efficiency above 100% is impossible, which rules out 125%. The value 32% reads the mechanical advantage of 3.2 as a percentage, and 125% would mean the machine gives out more work than it takes in.

questions.prompt: A solid weighs 4.0 N in air and 2.5 N when fully immersed in water. Its relative density is about
questions.explanation: Loss in weight = 1.5 N, so relative density = 4.0 / 1.5 = 2.7. Using the apparent weight as the loss gives 1.6, which is wrong.

questions.prompt: A density bottle weighs 20 g empty, 70 g full of water and 60 g full of a liquid. The relative density of the liquid is
questions.explanation: Mass of liquid = 40 g, mass of water = 50 g, so relative density = 40 / 50 = 0.80. The inverted ratio, 1.25, would describe a liquid denser than water.

questions.prompt: A ticker-tape timer powered by a 50 Hz supply makes a dot on the tape every
questions.explanation: Time between dots = 1 / 50 = 0.02 s. This is the basis for working out the speed from the dot spacing. The value 0.05 s is the interval for a 20 Hz supply.

questions.prompt: On a ticker tape, dots that are equally spaced show that the trolley was moving
questions.explanation: Equal spacing in equal times means constant speed. Increasing spacing would show acceleration.

questions.prompt: A block just begins to slide down a rough plane when the plane is tilted to 45 degrees. The coefficient of limiting friction is
questions.explanation: At the point of slipping, mu = tan(theta), and tan 45 degrees = 1.0. The value 0.71 is sin 45, which confuses the two functions.

questions.prompt: To reduce the effect of reaction time when timing a pendulum, it is best to

options.text: time one oscillation with great care
start the stopwatch before releasing the bob
time 20 oscillations and divide the total by 20

questions.explanation: Reaction time adds the same small error to the total, so a longer total makes it a smaller share of the result. One carefully timed oscillation still carries the full reaction-time error as a large share, and a long string lengthens the period without removing the timing error.

questions.prompt: A stopwatch with a reaction error of 0.2 s times 10 oscillations of a 1 s pendulum. The percentage error in the total time is about
questions.explanation: Percentage error = 0.2 / 10 x 100 = 2%. Timing a single swing would give 20%, which shows why many oscillations are timed.

questions.prompt: In a Hooke's law experiment, a graph of load against extension curves away from a straight line beyond a certain load. This point marks the

options.text: centre of gravity of the spring

questions.explanation: Past that point the extension is no longer proportional to the load, and the spring may not return to its original length.

questions.prompt: A trolley covers 2.0 m in 4.0 s at constant speed. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 2.0 / 4.0 = 0.50 m/s. Multiplying the figures gives 8.0, which confuses the operation.

questions.prompt: In a Young's modulus experiment on a wire, the diameter of the wire is best measured with a

options.text: micrometer screw gauge, at several points along the wire
metre rule, once at the middle

questions.explanation: The cross-section area depends on the diameter, so it needs a precise instrument and repeated readings, because wires are not uniform.

questions.prompt: The volume of an irregular stone that will not fit in a measuring cylinder can be found using

options.text: a displacement (eureka) can and a measuring cylinder

questions.explanation: The water displaced by the submerged stone is collected and measured, and its volume equals the stone's volume. A vernier caliper measures length, not the volume of an irregular shape, a stopwatch and ruler give no volume, and a spring balance measures weight.

questions.prompt: Before using a beam balance to weigh a sample, the user should first

options.text: place the heaviest mass on the pan
check that it reads zero with nothing on the pan and adjust if needed
tap the sample to remove dust

questions.explanation: A balance with a zero error gives every reading the same error, so it must be zeroed first. Placing the heaviest mass first or skipping levelling adds errors, and tapping the sample does nothing about the instrument's zero.

questions.prompt: When a wire is stretched in a laboratory experiment, safety requires that

options.text: the wire is stretched until it breaks
goggles are worn and a soft pad is placed under the hanging masses
masses are hung without any pad
students stand directly beneath the load

questions.explanation: A wire can snap and fling pieces, and the load can fall, so eyes and feet must be protected. Stretching the wire to breaking, hanging masses with no pad and standing under the load each invite injury.
